description: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman says New York would no longer be a sanctuary state if he is elected. The Nassau County Executive says he won't let Zohran Mamdani ruin New York City as mayor and he says President Donald Trump's tariffs help even the playing field for American businesses. He speaks to Joe Mathieu on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Bruce Blakeman on Tariffs, Hochul, Mamdani, Immigration

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Anthony Capaccio
description: President Donald Trump said he is considering limited military strikes to pressure Iran into signing a new nuclear deal, but bombing the country may have the opposite effect, risking a new destabilizing conflict in the Middle East.
title: Trump’s Threatened Strikes to Compel Iran Deal Risk Backfiring

description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta reacts to the Supreme Court decision striking down President Donald Trump's tariffs, describing the ruling as expected and affirming. Bonta highlights that the Court's ruling allows for retroactive relief, meaning businesses and importers who paid these tariffs can seek refunds through the Court of International Trade. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Tariff Ruling Calls Out Trump's 'Unlawfulness,' California AG Says

description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman, a City University of New York professor, says President Donald Trump's tariffs are a sales tax and are slightly contractionary. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Tariffs Are a Sales Tax, Krugman Says

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: After the Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump’s global tariffs, the president sought different legal grounds to get them back up.
title: Court Puts Up Tariff Roadblock. Trump Says He’ll Drive New Route

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the Supreme Court's ruling on President Trump's use of global tariffs. On today's show, Bloomberg Chief Political Correspondent Annmarie Hordern and Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Supreme Court Axes Trump Tariffs | Balance of Power: Early Edition 2/20/2026

author: Allyson Versprille
description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said he will brief lawmakers on Capitol Hill next week about the temporary closure of airspace around El Paso, Texas, earlier this month.
title: Duffy Will Brief Congress Next Week on El Paso Shutdown

author: Katie Greifeld
description: The Tuttle Capital UFO Disclosure ETF invests in forward-thinking technology
title: Trump to Release the UFO Files. There’s Somehow an ETF for That

description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says that revenue collected from tariffs will be little changed in 2026, despite Friday’s Supreme Court ruling, as President Donald Trump uses alternate authorities to impose duties. He speaks at the Economic Club of Dallas. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Bessent Says Tariff Revenue Will Be Little Changed in 2026

author: Thomas Seal
description: Canadian businesses can’t relax in light of the US Supreme Court decision striking down President Donald Trump’s emergency tariffs, experts said — the ruling simply moves his America First trade policy into a volatile new phase.
title: Canada Faces New, Unpredictable Trump Tools After Tariff Ruling

description: The Pentagon is pushing to develop a domestic supply of antimony, a metal critical to making weapons and often found alongside gold. That may be a bonanza for billionaire Trump supporter John Paulson. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Ally May Make Billions on Public Land

description: President Donald Trump says other alternatives “will now be used to replace the ones that the court incorrectly rejected" during a news conference following the Supreme Court's decision to strike down the Trump administration's tariffs.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Alternatives Will Be Used to Replace Rejected Tariffs

description: President Donald Trump says he is ashamed of certain Supreme Court justices for “not having the courage to do what’s right for our country” after the court struck down the Trump administration's tariffs. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Calls Supreme Court Tariff Ruling 'Deeply Disappointing'

author: Thomas Escritt
description: Hungary will block the release of a €90 billion ($106 billion) loan to Ukraine agreed by the European Union until shipments of Russian oil through the country resume, Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto said on Friday.
title: Hungary Says Will Block Loan to Ukraine Until Oil Flows Resume

description: Speaking in December, Peter Navarro told Mishal Husain the Trump administration has a "plan B" on tariffs. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Peter Navarro on Tariffs 'Plan B'

author: Michael B Marois
description: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed legislation authorizing the state to lend $590 million to keep major public-transit operators around San Francisco running as post-pandemic travel patterns continue to strain their finances.
title: California Lending $590 Million to Keep Bay Area Transit Running

description: Bloomberg Television recently traveled to Venezuela with Energy Secretary Chris Wright as he became the highest ranking US official in the country since the capture of Nicolás Maduro. Annmarie Hordern got a rare look into the country as it tries to rebuild. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Inside the US Effort to Rebuild Venezuela's Oil Industry

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: President Donald Trump is taking his pressure campaign against Cuba to Europe, mounting a renewed US push for Italy to halt its use of doctors from the struggling Caribbean nation.
title: Trump Targets Italy in His Push to Halt Cuba’s Export of Doctors

author: Sergio Mendoza, James Attwood
description: Bolivia’s state steel company is feuding with the Chinese engineering firm that built its flagship plant, and says it may seek to deduct some of the $100 million in losses from repayments to its lender, the Export-Import Bank of China.
title: Bolivia Steelmaker Weighs Deducting Mill Losses From China Loan

description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Matt Miller and Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." A major ruling from the Supreme Court as President Trump’s global tariffs were struck down in a decision that could reshape US trade and global markets. Bloomberg Open Interest hosts a panel of experts who break down what's at stake and what's next. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Tariffs Ruled Unlawful | Open Interest 2/20/2026

author: Gonzalo Soto, Carla Ros
description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is applying renewed pressure on Peru to allow an ideological ally to exit the South American nation, after the country inaugurated a new left-leaning leader.
title: Mexico Renews Push on Peru to Allow Departure of Holed-Up Ex PM

author: Alicia Diaz
description: President Donald Trump faces daunting odds of convincing the US Congress to restore his sweeping global tariffs after the Supreme Court decision Friday that struck them down.
title: Trump Faces Strong Resistance in Congress to Restoring Tariffs

author: Joe Mayes
description: London’s Metropolitan Police said it is investigating whether UK airports were used to facilitate the crimes of the disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein, as the fallout from the Epstein files continues to spread.
title: UK Police Probe If British Airports Used for Epstein Trafficking

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump will hold a press briefing after the Supreme Court struck down the bulk of the sweeping global tariffs he’s implemented in his second term, delivering a major blow against his signature economic policy.
title: Trump to Hold Press Briefing Following Court’s Tariff Ruling

author: Jorge Valero
description: European Union lawmakers will hold an emergency meeting Monday to reassess the bloc’s trade deal with the US following the Supreme Court’s decision to strike down some of President Donald Trump’s global tariffs.
title: EU Lawmakers Call Meeting on US Trade Deal After Tariff Ruling

author: Antonia Mufarech, Carolina Gonzalez
description: The US slapped visa restrictions on a Chilean cabinet minister and two other government officials in an apparent rebuke over the country’s close trade relationship with China.
title: Chile Minister Among Officials Hit With US Visa Restrictions

author: Isabel Gottlieb, Laura Curtis, Zoe Tillman
description: Tariff refunds for companies that paid tens of billions were left unresolved by the Supreme Court, which ruled on Friday that President Donald Trump didn’t have legal authority to impose the duties under an emergency law.
title: Tariff Ruling Kicks Off Messy Fight Over $170 Billion in Refunds

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Kate Sullivan
description: US President Donald Trump plans to travel to China from March 31 to April 2 for a meeting with his counterpart Xi Jinping as the two leaders will look to navigate a trade relationship again plunged into uncertainty and navigate tensions around Taiwan.
title: Trump Will Travel to China in Late March for High-Stakes Xi Meet

description: The US Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s global tariffs, saying he exceeded his authority. Bloomberg's Nathan Dean and Mike McKee discuss how President Trump may respond to the decision on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How Will Trump Respond to the Supreme Court Tariff Ruling?

description: The US Supreme Court in Washington. Photographer: Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg
title: US Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump Global Tariffs

author: Greg Stohr
description: The US Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s sweeping global tariffs, undercutting his signature economic policy and delivering his biggest legal defeat since he returned to the White House.
title: Trump’s Global Tariffs Struck Down by US Supreme Court

author: Eric Laperozy
description: Madagascan President Michael Randrianirina, who came to power in a coup last year, has broken tradition by visiting Russia rather than former colonial power France on his first official trip abroad.
title: Madagascan President Breaks Tradition With First Trip to Moscow

author: Francois de Beaupuy
description: US Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings Inc. completed its purchase of a majority stake in a data center unit owned by Electricite de France SA, with the government signing off on condition that a French investor take a stake.
title: France Clears Sale of EDF Data Center Unit to Bitcoin Miner MARA

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump said he’s considering a limited military strike on Iran, ramping up pressure on the regime as he masses military forces in the region and his envoys push for a deal to limit its nuclear program.
title: Trump Won’t Rule Out Limited Iran Strike as Forces Gather

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: President Donald Trump said that last year’s government shutdown cost the US “at least two points in GDP” in a social media post less than an hour before the government was expected to release the first estimate of the fourth-quarter change in inflation-adjusted gross domestic product.
title: Trump Bemoans Shutdown Impact on GDP Before Fourth Quarter Read

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: The International Monetary Fund’s board will meet on February 26 to consider a four-year, $8.1 billion loan program for Ukraine, people familiar with the matter said.
title: IMF’s Board Said to Meet to Consider Ukraine’s Loan on Feb. 26

author: Taylan Bilgic
description: A Turkish court has formally arrested Alican Uludag, a correspondent for the Turkish service of Germany’s state-funded broadcaster Deutsche Welle, on a charge of insulting President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
title: Turkey Arrests Deutsche Welle Reporter for ‘Insulting President’

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: Senator Elizabeth Warren is demanding that Federal Reserve nominees commit to protect independent research after National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said the authors of a New York Fed study that found US firms and consumers paid nearly 90% of the cost of tariffs should be “disciplined.”
title: Warren Demands Trump’s Fed Nominees Vow to Protect Research

author: Sankalp Phartiyal
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi made his pitch this week that India can play a leading role in the artificial intelligence boom with a conference featuring tech stars from around the world. It suffered more than a few hitches.
title: Modi’s Chaotic AI Summit Showed India’s Clout and Constraints

author: Anuradha Raghu
description: Malaysia’s leading civil society groups are urging the formation of a Royal Commission of Inquiry to investigate allegations surrounding abuse of power, unexplained wealth and regulatory extortion by the country’s anti-graft agency and its chief Azam Baki.
title: Malaysia Civil Groups Say Royal Commission Should Probe MACC

author: Nojoud Al Mallees
description: More than half of Canadians say the US currently poses the greatest threat to their country’s security, a stark indicator of how wide the perceived rift has become between the historically close allies.
title: US Poses Greater Security Threat Than China, Canadians Say in Poll

author: Alan Crawford
description: America has been spared the reckoning seen elsewhere despite known ties to the disgraced financier.
title: Epstein Impact Hits Everywhere But US Politics

author: Jonathan Tirone
description: US President Donald Trump’s warning to Iran — that it has just 10 to 15 days to avert potential military action — suggests matters could come to a head when the United Nations nuclear watchdog next meets to decide whether to further censure the Islamic Republic.
title: Trump Iran Ultimatum Sets Up Attacks Following IAEA Meeting

author: Suzanne Lynch, Stephen Carroll (Radio), Caroline Hepker
description: US President Donald Trump’s envoy to the European Union denounced a forthcoming “Made in Europe” plan, warning that it could damage allies’ defense efforts and weaken Ukraine’s ability to fight Russia.
title: US Envoy Warns ‘Made In Europe’ Plan Will Damage Allied Defense

author: Fabienne Kinzelmann
description: President Donald Trump said his tariffs spurred Novartis AG to expand its US manufacturing footprint, following a meeting with the Swiss drugmaker’s chief executive Vas Narasimhan at the White House on Wednesday.
title: Trump Says Tariffs Pushed Novartis to Expand Operations in US

author: Stacey Vanek Smith
description: The Fed chair is deploying strategies to help fortify the 112-year-old institution’s independence.
title: How Jerome Powell Is Trump-Proofing the Fed

author: Arne Delfs
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz delivered a rousing speech at a congress of his Christian Democratic Union in Stuttgart in which he sought to rally the party behind his vision for Germany ahead of a vote on his leadership later on Friday.
title: Merz Seeks to Rally CDU Amid Entrenched German Voter Skepticism

author: Michael Nienaber
description: Germany denied a Reuters report that said the government in Berlin was in talks to purchase additional Lockheed Martin Corp. F-35 fighter-jets on top of an existing order of 35 aircraft.
title: Germany Denies Report on Plan to Buy Additional US F-35 Fighters

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, the US military is stationing a vast array of forces in the Middle East, including two aircraft carriers, fighter jets and refueling tankers, as President Donald Trump says Iran has 10 to 15 days to strike a deal over its nuclear program

Oil rose to the highest since August after President Trump issued the deadline. 

Trump ordered the US to release files about aliens and UFOs. He earlier accused Barack Obama of giving away classified information in a recent podcast.

Today's guests: Rabobank FX Strategy Head Jane Foley & US Ambassador To The EU Andrew Puzder. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US-Iran: Trump Gives Tehran 10 to 15 Days for Nuclear Deal | Daybreak Europe 02/20/2026

author: Shoko Oda, Josh Saul, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump’s $33 billion deal with Japan to build the largest US gas power project in Ohio hasn’t secured binding commitments, still needs to lock in equipment suppliers and was a complete surprise to the state’s regulator and grid operator.
title: Trump’s $33 Billion Ohio Gas Project Is Very Short on Details

description: President Donald Trump said on Thursday Iran has 10 to 15 days at most to agree to a deal over its nuclear program. His comments came as the US military is stationing a vast array of forces in the Middle East in a deployment not seen since 2003 ahead of the invasion of Iraq, suggesting Trump is giving himself discretion to launch a sustained campaign lasting many days. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Gives Iran 10 to 15 Days for Nuclear Deal

author: Julian Harris, Andrew Atkinson, Philip Aldrick
description: Rachel Reeves’ future was in the balance this time last year — Britain’s borrowing costs had surged, forcing the Chancellor of the Exchequer to consider more tax hikes or spending cuts. Still, she survived and one year on the UK economy is treating the Labour government to some pleasant surprises.
title: Reeves Gets Boost From Trio of Economist-Defying UK Data Points

description: Oil rose to a six-month high as escalating tensions in Iran weighed on risk sentiment. The commodity is up more than 6% this week to $72 a barrel after US President Donald Trump said Iran had 15 days at most to reach a deal over its nuclear program. Bloomberg's Anthony di Paola reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Hits Six-Month High Amid US-Iran Tensions

author: Samy Adghirni, Mark Schroers
description: Europe is rushing to safeguard its most critical institutions ahead of a presidential election in France in which surveys show a commanding lead for the far-right National Rally.
title: France’s Ascendant Far Right Has Europe Seeking Out Firewalls

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: Spain is planning to build more political and financial links to China as US President Donald Trump upends the global economic order.
title: Spain Courts China in New Asia Strategy as US Ties Sour

description: James Jeffrey, former US ambassador to Iraq and Turkey, says President Trump wants a "real deal" with Iran and "is willing to roll the dice on military action." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Wants a 'Real' Iran Nuclear Deal, Former US Ambassador Says

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Daniela Milanese, Martha Viotti Beck
description: Brazil and India are set to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals and artificial intelligence when President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva meets Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as the two nations position themselves as leading voices for the developing world amid a fragile global order.
title: Brazil and India to Deepen Critical Mineral and Technology Ties

author: Ken Parks, Ignacio Olivera Doll
description: Latin America stands to benefit from President Donald Trump’s greater involvement, said Paraguay President Santiago Peña, who has emerged as one of the staunchest US allies in the region.
title: Paraguay’s President Backs Trump’s New Monroe Doctrine In Latin America

author: Kok Leong Chan, Ram Anand
description: The Democratic Action Party, the largest party in Malaysia’s ruling coalition, will decide in July whether to retain its cabinet posts or move to the backbenches in Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s administration, in a move that could signal shifts in Chinese support for the premier.
title: Malaysia’s Top Coalition Party Weighs Cabinet Roles, Report Says

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: US and Chinese fighter jets briefly faced off above waters near the Korean Peninsula this week, Yonhap News reported, marking a rare confrontation in that area between the two superpowers.
title: US, China Jets Briefly Face Off Near Korea, Yonhap Says

author: Anna J Kaiser
description: The Palm Beach airport will soon be renamed after Donald Trump, making it the latest institution to bear the name of the president.
title: Palm Beach Airport to Be Named Donald J. Trump International

author: Andreina Itriago
description: The Venezuelan government approved a much-awaited amnesty law that could free hundreds of political prisoners, after adding carveouts that would leave many to deal with a largely distrusted court system and likely exclude many opposition leaders from benefiting.
title: Venezuela’s Amnesty Law Passes With Huge Caveats

author: Mark Schroers, Alexander Weber
description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde reiterated calls for global partnership to salvage an international order that not only benefits the strongest.
title: ECB’s Lagarde Renews Call for Cooperation to Save Global Order

author: Hadriana Lowenkron, Maggie Eastland
description: The Trump administration is planning a new Peace Corps initiative that would send thousands of US science and math graduates abroad to boost foreign countries’ reliance on American technology and reduce global adoption of competing products from China, according to a US official.
title: US Plans Peace Corps Revamp to Gain Edge in AI Race With China
